text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- False working papers have been issued to 4,000 Bosnian Serb refugees living in the disputed town of Brcko, says Mirsad Dzapo, a Moslem-Croat federation official. He said Serb authorities are abusing rules for upcoming local elections which allow anyone legally employed in Brcko to vote.
- Rules for local elections will cause Bosnia to lose control of its state border around Brcko and allow Serb authorities to remain in control, says former Brcko mayor, Munib Jusufovic.

- International superviser for Brcko, Robert Farrand, and chief of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in Bosnia, Robert Frowick, plan to meet federation delegation in northern Bosnia on Monday to discuss threat by federation to boycott municipal elections in Brcko.
- If Bosnian Croat proposal on forming new municipalities in central Bosnia is approved by the federation parliament, that would split federation territory in two halves, newspaper commentary says.

- Some 90,000 refugees returned last year out of which 8,000 moved back to Bosnia's Serb republic. During the same period 150,000 displaced persons went back to their homes, ministry for refugees of Sarajevo canton says in a statement.

- The Bosnian Serb army has destroyed only 2.5 percent of its arms surplus and thus violated terms of the Dayton peace agreement, says General Ramiz Drekovic, Bosnian army representative to OSCE commission for military balance.
- Bosnia is a small country but the conflict which is still under way here is not. That is why NATO must stay in Bosnia, commentary says.
- Elections in Brcko will not influence an arbitration decision for the town, says Robert Farrand, international supervisor for the town. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387 71 663 864
